records.quote: there burst up from that doomed and accursed farm a gleamingly eruptive cataclysm of unnatural sparks and substance; blurring the glance of the few who saw it, and sending forth to the zenith a bombarding cloudburst of such coloured and fantastic fragments as our universe must needs disown
records.paraphrase: The farm erupts in a cataclysm of unnatural sparks and coloured fragments after the colour departs.

records.quote: the poor woman screamed about things in the air which she could not describe. In her raving there was not a single specific noun, but only verbs and pronouns.
records.paraphrase: Mrs. Gardner goes mad, raving about indescribable things in the air.

records.quote: The swine began growing grey and brittle and falling to pieces before they died, and their eyes and muzzles developed singular alterations.
records.paraphrase: Livestock sicken, turning grey and brittle and disintegrating before death.

records.quote: Under the spectroscope both samples gave off an unknown spectrum, in which many of the baffling bands were precisely like those which the strange meteor had yielded in the previous year. The property of emitting this spectrum vanished in a month, the dust thereafter consisting mainly of alkaline phosphates and carbonates.
records.paraphrase: Laboratory analysis links the dust samples to the meteor via matching spectroscopic bands that later fade.

records.quote: A dim though distinct luminosity seemed to inhere in all the vegetation, grass, leaves, and blossoms alike, while at one moment a detached piece of the phosphorescence appeared to stir furtively in the yard near the barn.
records.paraphrase: All the vegetation begins to glow faintly, and a piece of phosphorescence seems to move on its own.

records.quote: Into the fine flavour of the pears and apples had crept a stealthy bitterness and sickishness, so that even the smallest of bites induced a lasting disgust. It was the same with the melons and tomatoes, and Nahum sadly saw that his entire crop was lost.
records.paraphrase: The fruit and crops grow large but become inedibly bitter, and the entire harvest is ruined.

records.quote: The professors tried it with a geologist's hammer and found it was oddly soft. It was, in truth, so soft as to be almost plastic; and they gouged rather than chipped a specimen to take back to the college for testing.
records.paraphrase: University professors examine the meteorite and take a specimen to the college for testing.

records.quote: Then without warning the hideous thing shot vertically up toward the sky like a rocket or meteor, leaving behind no trail and disappearing through a round and curiously regular hole in the clouds before any man could gasp or cry out.
records.paraphrase: The colour entity shoots up into the sky and departs through the clouds toward space.

records.quote: the cleft, bulging lips were just able to crackle out a final answer.
records.paraphrase: Nahum, dying and disintegrating, manages a final answer to Ammi.

records.quote: It was nothing of this earth, but a piece of the great outside; and as such dowered with outside properties and obedient to outside laws.
records.paraphrase: The scientists conclude the substance is not of earth and follows laws foreign to earthly physics.

records.quote: It was just a colour out of space\u2014a frightful messenger from unformed realms of infinity beyond all Nature as we know it
records.paraphrase: The narrator frames the phenomenon as a colour from outside all known Nature.

records.quote: the great rock that fell out of the sky and bedded itself in the ground beside the well at the Nahum Gardner place
records.paraphrase: A meteorite arrives from the sky and embeds itself on the farm, introducing an object of extraterrestrial origin.

records.quote: no other name could fit such thing, or any other thing fit such a name. It was as if the poet had coined the phrase from having seen this one particular region. It must, I thought as I viewed it, be the outcome of a fire; but why had nothing new ever grown over those five acres of grey desolation that sprawled open to the sky like a great spot eaten by acid in the woods and fields?
records.paraphrase: A five-acre expanse of grey desolation where nothing grows exists as a permanent alteration to the landscape.

records.quote: In terms of matter I suppose the thing Ammi described would be called a gas, but this gas obeyed laws that are not of our cosmos.
records.paraphrase: The narrator contrasts the entity with known matter, noting it obeyed laws outside our cosmos.

records.quote: The stone, magnetic as it had been, must have had some peculiar electrical property; for it had "drawn the lightning," as Nahum said, with a singular persistence. Six times within an hour the farmer saw the lightning strike the furrow in the front yard
records.paraphrase: The meteorite's magnetic and electrical properties are said to have repeatedly drawn lightning to the yard.

records.quote: when upon heating before the spectroscope it displayed shining bands unlike any known colours of the normal spectrum there was much breathless talk of new elements, bizarre optical properties, and other things which puzzled men of science are wont to say when faced by the unknown
records.paraphrase: Spectroscopic testing reveals bands unlike any known spectrum, prompting talk of new elements and bizarre optical properties.

records.quote: Hot as it was, they tested it in a crucible with all the proper reagents. Water did nothing. Hydrochloric acid was the same. Nitric acid and even aqua regia merely hissed and spattered against its torrid invulnerability.
records.paraphrase: Scientists systematically test the meteorite with a series of reagents and acids, none of which affect it.

records.quote: it must be some'at growed from a round ball like one we all seen in the meteor stone that fell a year ago June. Sucks an' burns, he said, an' is jest a cloud of colour like that light out thar now
records.paraphrase: Ammi explains the entity grew from the globule in the meteor and appears as a life-draining cloud of colour.

records.quote: All the orchard trees blossomed forth in strange colours, and through the stony soil of the yard and adjacent pasturage there sprang up a bizarre growth which only a botanist could connect with the proper flora of the region.
records.paraphrase: The vegetation develops strange colors and bizarre growth unrelated to the region's normal flora.

records.quote: Botanists, too, ought to study the stunted flora on the borders of that spot, for they might shed light on the country notion that the blight is spreading\u2014little by little, perhaps an inch a year.
records.paraphrase: The blight is said to continue spreading outward at roughly an inch per year.

criteria.rationale: The story materially deploys spectroscopy, unknown spectral bands, magnetism, meteoric iron (Widmanstatten figures), and speculation about new elements. The scientific analysis of the meteorite and dust is central to framing the phenomenon as a substance obedient to 'outside laws.'

Laboratory apparatus (spectroscope, crucible, reagents) appears, but no engineered device or invention materially affects the setting, problem, or outcome. The tools are ordinary scientific instruments used for analysis, not a plot-driving invention. The threat is a cosmic entity, not a technology.

The story is set in a mundane historical New England (the 1880s) with a frame in the near-present. There is no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement. The extraterrestrial origin of the meteor relates to other places, not to time travel or a displaced era.

From the identifiable premise of an alien meteoric substance contaminating the soil, the story systematically develops escalating consequences: bitter crops, chromatic and monstrous flora, luminous vegetation, disintegrating livestock, human madness and death, and a permanent spreading blight. This extrapolated cascade is the spine of the narrative.

Professors conduct systematic testing: gouging specimens, applying a series of reagents and acids, heating, spectroscopy, and later comparative analysis of dust samples matching the meteor's spectral bands. This observation, measurement, and comparative inference materially drives the reader's understanding, even as the entity ultimately eludes classification.

The core threat is a visitor from a nonordinary cosmic environment: a colour out of space, a messenger from realms beyond Nature obedient to laws not of our cosmos, arriving via meteorite and departing back into the sky. This extra-cosmic visitor is the central novum.

The alien contamination is a causally central, large-scale biological/cosmic disaster: it wipes out an entire family and their livestock, sterilizes five acres into a permanent 'blasted heath,' culminates in an eruptive cataclysm, and continues spreading. The catastrophe is both actual and impending (the ongoing blight).

candidates.description:
An extraterrestrial entity
described as a 'colour out of space'
delivered by a meteorite, an amorphous life-draining presence that obeys laws foreign to our cosmos. It manifests as an indescribable colour, drains and corrupts all living things around the Gardner farm, and ultimately departs, leaving a permanent zone of grey desolation ('the blasted heath').

novelty.rationale: The entity is a totalizing difference from the empirical norm: a form of matter/energy obeying laws 'not of our cosmos,' a colour outside the known spectrum and beyond all Nature as we know it. It permanently alters the storyworld, producing five acres of grey desolation where nothing grows and a blight that spreads.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The phenomenon is presented through systematic, immanent, nonsupernatural inquiry: professors apply the geologist's hammer, spectroscope, reagents and acids, and later police laboratory analysis matches the dust's spectrum to the meteor's. It is explicitly framed as an unknown but material entity ('a gas'), obeying alien but lawful physics rather than magic or the divine. The story develops a coherent imaginary-science logic (growth from globule, feeding on life, silicon affinity, spectral bands that fade).

narrative_hegemony.rationale:
The colour governs the entire narrative logic. Every major event
decline of crops, madness of the family, death of livestock and humans, the well phenomena, the final eruption and departure, and the enduring blasted heath
flows directly from it. It is not an incidental gadget but the overriding organizing force of the whole tale.

estrangement.rationale: Reader-facing estrangement is generated by the narrator's insistence that the entity is a colour and gas obeying laws outside our cosmos, a messenger from realms beyond all Nature. Storyworld consequences (poisoned crops, mutated flora, disintegrating livestock and humans, permanent blasted heath, spreading blight) and character reactions (Mrs. Gardner's noun-less raving, Nahum's dying testimony) mark the estranging contrast with the empirical norm.

candidates.description: The meteorite itself: an anomalous stone from stellar space that is soft/plastic, retains heat, is magnetic, draws lightning, resists all reagents, wastes away, shows an unknown spectrum, and contains coloured globules.

novelty.rationale:
The stone exhibits properties foreign to earthly matter
non-volatile, resistant to all acids, wasting away, unknown spectrum, obedient to 'outside laws.' It is a genuine difference from the empirical norm.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The stone is subjected to a coherent, systematic, nonsupernatural investigation with reagents, spectroscope, and geological tools, and is rationalized as an object obeying alien but lawful physics.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The meteorite is the delivery vehicle and dissipates early; it is not the force that governs the narrative. The driving agent of all consequences is the colour entity that emerges from the globule. The stone is best understood as an incidental precursor device subordinate to the colour novum, not the overriding narrative logic itself.

estrangement.rationale: The stone estranges via its impossible material behavior under laboratory testing, but its story-level consequences are mediated entirely through the colour it releases rather than the stone as such.
